minutes.headline: Board held the historic district guidelines for owner notice; appointed a full-time officer and new town counsel.
minutes.summary: The board appointed a new full-time police officer, discussed a fee waiver for a memorial fieldhouse, and heard concerns about a restaurant's lapsed workers' comp coverage. It discussed the draft historic district guidelines at length and agreed to bring them back after notice to property owners. It also made annual appointments, kept the animal control officer matter for a future agenda, and approved a town counsel contract after executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board held the draft historic district guidelines to return after revisions and notice to property owners; a motion to postpone was withdrawn.
The board appointed a full-time police officer, effective July 1, 2017; the vote tally was not audible in the recording.
The board took up a request to waive the building permit fee for a memorial foundation's fieldhouse, with members asking about precedent and cost.
After executive session, the board approved a town counsel services contract effective July 1.
Concerns about the animal control officer were set for a future agenda, and the annual town manager appointments were ratified, subject to held positions.

why_it_matters: The historic district guidelines could affect what owners may do with their property, and the board has said owners will be notified before the guidelines return.
A permit fee waiver for the fieldhouse sets a precedent that members questioned, and a waived fee is revenue the town does not collect.
The van reimbursement is changing to a share of driver payroll, and a shortfall is covered in the FY18 budget by appropriation and formula grant funds.
watch_next: The historic district guidelines returning to the board after revisions and notice to property owners.
The animal control officer matter on a future board agenda.
